sections.heading: C — Learner permit, license tests and license classes (North Carolina)
sections.markdown:
## C — Learner permit, license tests and license classes (North Carolina)
Knowledge domain: who needs which license, what each license test checks, and how vehicle weight sets the license class.

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
In North Carolina it is illegal to drive a motor vehicle on public streets and highways unless you hold a valid driver license; driving is a legal privilege that comes with responsibility. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Without a valid license you also may not sit behind the wheel while the engine is running, or steer a vehicle while another vehicle pushes or tows it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Typical office hours run Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m., though some small-town offices open only on certain days. [A01]
Why it matters: dynamic fact; hours change, so learners should confirm current hours on the DMV website.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
You can book a license exam appointment online, but you do not need one; walk-in customers are served all day until the office is full. [A01]
Why it matters: dynamic fact; scheduling methods can change.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
A regular learner permit is available to anyone who is 18 years old or older. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A01
A learner permit lets its holder drive the type or class of vehicle it names, but only while the permit is in the holder's possession. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A01
When a permit holder drives on the highway, a person licensed for that vehicle must ride in the seat beside them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A01
To get a learner permit you must pass a vision check, a traffic signs test and a test on motor vehicle laws. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A01
Applicants for any original driver license may be tested on vision, motor vehicle law knowledge, traffic signs, and driving skill in an on-road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A01
A motorcycle learner permit applicant aged 16 to 17 must already hold a full provisional license and have a parent or guardian sign; an applicant 18 or older must already hold a license from the division. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A02
Every driver license test is scored on its own, so you must pass each one separately. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A02
Your vision is checked whenever you apply in person, whether for a learner permit, an original license or a renewal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A02
If you need glasses or contacts to meet the vision standard, you must wear them every time you drive, and your license will carry a corrective-lens restriction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A02
Driving without the corrective lenses your license requires is punished the same way as driving with no license at all. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A02
On the signs test you must recognize each traffic sign by its color and shape and say what it means; every sign on that test appears in the handbook. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A02
The knowledge test covers traffic laws and safe driving practices, and an audio version can be requested by applicants who struggle with reading. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A02
The on-road driving test comes last, after every other test is passed; it is required for a first license, may be required at renewal, and is never required for a learner permit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A02
During the road test you show that you can perform basic driving patterns and drive safely in traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A02
A person whose mental or physical condition could make driving unsafe may be denied a license, while a person with a disability can get a restricted license if the condition does not prevent safe driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A02
CDL Class A, B or C applicants study the CDL Handbook, and motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle permit applicants study the Motorcycle Handbook. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A03
Road-test examiners grade how you approach intersections, stop signs and signals; quick stops on command; backing; stopping, starting and parking; clutch use in a manual car; turn signals and horn; turning; lane use; following; passing and being passed; yielding to pedestrians and vehicles; posture; and the three-point turnabout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A03
Original license applicants must take the on-road test, although the handbook notes some cases where it may not be required. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A03
North Carolina issues both a regular driver license and a commercial driver license, and the vehicle you will drive decides which class you need. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A03
You must take the driving skills test in a vehicle that represents the license class you are applying for. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A03
A regular Class A license covers a CDL-exempt vehicle combination whose towed unit has a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,001 pounds or more. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A03
A regular Class B license covers a CDL-exempt single vehicle rated at 26,001 pounds or more, including when it tows a vehicle rated no more than 10,000 pounds. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A03
A regular Class C license covers a noncommercial single vehicle rated under 26,001 pounds, and a towing combination rated under 26,001 pounds combined when the driver is at least 18. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A03
Most drivers only need a regular Class C license for personal cars and small trucks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A03
Three-point turnabout, step one: from the far right edge of the road, check for traffic, signal left, creep forward turning the wheel left, and stop several inches from the left curb or edge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A03
Three-point turnabout, step two: back up slowly while turning the wheel right, and stop several inches from the right curb or edge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A03
Three-point turnabout, step three: move forward slowly with the wheel turned left to complete the turnabout. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A04
A commercial driver license is required for paid or volunteer drivers of the listed vehicle types that are built or used to carry passengers or property. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A04
A commercial Class A vehicle is a combination with a combined weight rating of at least 26,001 pounds whose towed unit is rated at least 10,001 pounds. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A04
A commercial Class B vehicle is a single vehicle rated at least 26,001 pounds, or a combination whose towing unit is rated at least 26,001 pounds while the towed unit is rated under 10,001 pounds. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A04
A commercial Class C vehicle is one outside Classes A and B that is built to carry 16 or more people counting the driver, or that carries hazardous materials requiring placards. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A04
No CDL is needed for recreational vehicles, military equipment, fire or emergency equipment, or certain farm vehicles, but a regular license of the right class is always required. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A04
On-duty volunteer fire, rescue or EMS members may drive Class A, B or C fire-fighting, rescue or EMS vehicles while holding only a regular A, B or C license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A04
Hauling hazardous materials, carrying passengers, driving school or activity buses, pulling double trailers and driving tank vehicles each require a special CDL endorsement. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A04
To operate a motorcycle on public roads, a person needs a motorcycle learner permit or a regular or commercial license carrying a motorcycle endorsement. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A04
A school bus driver must be at least 18, have at least six months of driving experience, and hold a Class B or C CDL with S and P endorsements plus a School Bus Driver's Certificate; activity bus drivers meet the same terms without the certificate. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A04
Under G.S. 20-37.14A, the division will not issue or renew a CDL with a P or S endorsement for anyone who must register as a sex offender. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0013]

Misconceptions: a learner permit does not let you drive alone, since a licensed driver must sit beside you; passing the signs test does not excuse the knowledge test because each test is passed separately; the road test is never part of getting a learner permit; most car drivers need a regular Class C, not a CDL.
Mnemonics: road-test order is See, Sign, Know, Drive — vision, signs, knowledge, then the on-road test last. Turnabout is Left forward, Right back, Left forward.
Glossary: GVWR means gross vehicle weight rating, the maker's maximum loaded weight; CDL means commercial driver license; endorsement means an added permission printed on a license; restriction means a condition such as corrective lenses that limits a license.
Dynamic facts: office hours and online appointment booking are time-variable service details and are isolated as dynamic; confirm them on the DMV website before relying on them.
